Idioms.phrase: 9-to-5 - An average job schedule.
Idioms.definition: As in this example, He decided that he was going to look for a 9-to-5 job soon .

Idioms.phrase: A bad apple - A bad (or morally questionable) person within a group of good individuals, who might corrupt the entire group. Like a rotten apple in a barrel of good ones .
Idioms.definition: As in this example, Onlookers were worried that the entire group of trick-or-treaters was bad, but there were really only a couple of bad apples.

Idioms.phrase: A baker's dozen - Thirteen, or one more than an actual dozen (which is twelve).
Idioms.definition: As in this example, We went to the grocery store and bought a baker's dozen of chocolate chip muffins. We're looking forward to eating them later.

Idioms.phrase: A ballpark figure - An approximate figure.
Idioms.definition: As in this example, This is only a ballpark figure. It may not be very accurate once you add up all the numbers.

Idioms.phrase: A bird in the hand is worth two in the bush - What you have at this moment carries more value than something you might obtain later.
Idioms.definition: As in this example, Jane asked me whether she should take the current job offer or wait for a better one. I told her to accept the current one. After all, a bird in the hand is worth two in the bush.

Idioms.phrase: A bit/A little bit - To a small extent or a small amount.
Idioms.definition: As in this example, I think I'll have just a little bit of cereal this morning. I'm not very hungry.

Idioms.phrase: A blessing in disguise - Something that seems bad initially, but that ends up having a positive outcome.
Idioms.definition: As in this example, He was very upset about not getting the job, but it ended up being a blessing in disguise as he got a better one later on.

Idioms.phrase: A bone to pick - A reason why one is upset.
Idioms.definition: As in this example, I have a bone to pick with you. I don't like the way you did this.

Idioms.phrase: A breath of fresh air - A person who is different from others in a very positive way. Everyone thought that Sasha was a breath of fresh air. She was so clever and friendly, and so different from anyone else they'd ever met.
A bunch of friends and I are going on a day trip tomorrow.
Have you met Max? That guy has a real chip on his shoulder. He's always a bit arrogant and on the defensive.
Elizabeth tried to hand in her assignment, but her teacher said it was a day late and a dollar short.
Shirts in that style are a dime a dozen at the local mall.
That storm the other day was a real doozy! I don't think I'll ever forget it. The thunder was terrible.
Jonathan is very hard to convince about anything. He always wants evidence. He's a real doubting Thomas.
That movie was a far cry from anything I would like. I just didn't enjoy it.
The team decided that the additional guest speaker was a fifth wheel and not necessary to include.
We were excited about what happened, but it ended up just being a flash in the pan. Nothing came of it.
I can't believe so many people have bought the product from that questionable infomercial. Well, you know what they say! A fool and his money are easily parted.
I have to give the script writers an A for effort, but I don't feel that the program came together very well in the end.
I think I've reached a fork in the road here. I don't know which direction to go.
Shelly was always such a good Samaritan. She always helped people in need.
Helen tended to be difficult to deal with. She had a lot of hang-ups, and it was easy to offend her.
Yes, I'm enjoying my new job. My boss, though, is a hard nut to crack. I'm having difficulty in understanding what he wants.
The family tried to avoid bringing up political hot potatoes during the holidays.
The politician was known to be corrupt. It had been proven that he had accepted kickbacks from several people.
How did I find out that your sister is getting married? A little bird told me.
Some people are always promoting opinions that make me realize that a little learning can be a dangerous thing.
I can't believe I forgot that! I have a memory like a sieve.
You're very quiet today. A penny for your thoughts.
Try to save more of your money. Remember that a penny saved is a penny earned.
The family seemed to be experiencing a perfect storm of unfortunate events.
Look at the sad faces on everyone. They wouldn’t believe it if they hadn’t seen it. A picture is worth a thousand words.
Don't worry about the exam. I took one for the same course last year and it was a piece of cake.
Audrey is a ray of sunshine. She is always so cheerful that she inevitably cheers me up as well.

We thought he had a screw loose when we saw him dancing around as if his shoes were on fire!

You're a really smart cookie, so you're sure to do well on the test if you study hard.
Things started to go wrong; eventually, it seemed like they were dealing with a snowball effect.
Jake wants to travel this summer but there's not a snowball's chance in hell that he will get to.
Abby decided to deal with the problem and not leave it for later. After all, a stitch in time saves nine.
We had an awesome time on vacation! The hotel was just a stone's throw away from lots of the museums we were eager to visit.

I'm afraid I have a terrible sweet tooth. I eat far too much cake and candy.

I ended up ruining my knitting project. I'm all thumbs with complicated things like that.
